questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the logic table in Figure 1.

| $p$ | $q$ | $\sim q$ | $p \Rightarrow \sim q$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | | |
| T | F | | |
| F | T | | |
| F | F | | |

*Figure 1* *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Column $\sim q$:** the negation reverses the truth value of $q$.

**Column $p \Rightarrow \sim q$:** an implication is false only when $p$ is true and the conclusion $\sim q$ is false; in every other case it is true.

| $p$ | $q$ | $\sim q$ | $p \Rightarrow \sim q$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F |
| T | F | T | T |
| F | T | F | T |
| F | F | T | T |

*Note on the connective:* the symbol between $p$ and $\sim q$ is not printed legibly on the paper (a blank box). If it is read as **conjunction** ($p \wedge \sim q$) the column is F, T, F, F; if it is read as **disjunction** ($p \vee \sim q$) the column is T, T, F, T. The method is the same: complete $\sim q$ first, then apply the truth rule of the connective row by row.
